title: Canonical root tower pullback and tensor coherence
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the root sheaves $M_{s,T}=\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ with transitions $u\mapsto u^\ell$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], and let $L_T=\varprojlim_{s\geq1}M_{s,T}$ with projections $p_{s,T}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Put $Z_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$ and $R_{s,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^s)_T$, with constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $\ell$-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. The $Z_T$-action on $L_T$ is $(a x)_s=x_s^{a\bmod\ell^s}$, extended from constant scalars by sheafification. Use ordinary sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For a scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$ between such schemes, let $v^{-1}$ be pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and let $c^v_s:v^{-1}M_{s,T}\to M_{s,T'}$ be the canonical root map adjoint to pullback of units [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. Identify inverse images of constant rings with the target constant rings. The maps $c^v_s$ are semilinear for these ring maps, commute with power transitions, and obey identity and composition: $c^{\mathrm{id}}_s=\mathrm{id}$ and $c^{v\circ w}_s=c^w_s\,w^{-1}c^v_s$ under canonical inverse-image comparisons for $T''\xrightarrow{w}T'\xrightarrow{v}T$.

There is a unique $Z_{T'}$-linear map $c^v_L:v^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'}$ with
$$p_{s,T'}c^v_L=c^v_s\,v^{-1}p_{s,T}\qquad(s\geq1).$$
These maps obey $c^{\mathrm{id}}_L=\mathrm{id}$ and $c^{v\circ w}_L=c^w_L\,w^{-1}c^v_L$ under the same comparisons.

For any commutative $\mathbf Z_\ell$-algebra $B$, set $H_T=L_T\otimes_{Z_T}B_T$. Under canonical ordinary tensor pullback identifications, $c^v_L\otimes1$ induces the $B_{T'}$-linear map $h_v:v^*H_T\to H_{T'}$, given by $x\otimes b\mapsto c^v_L(x)\otimes b$. These maps obey identity and composition: $h_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $h_{v\circ w}=h_w\,w^*h_v$. For every $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rB=0$, put $D_{r,T}=M_{r,T}\otimes_{R_{r,T}}B_T$ and define $\alpha_{r,T}:H_T\to D_{r,T}$ by $x\otimes b\mapsto p_{r,T}(x)\otimes b$. Then the specified maps satisfy
$$\alpha_{r,T'}h_v=(c^v_r\otimes1)v^*\alpha_{r,T}.$$
This assertion does not assume that $\alpha_{r,T}$ or $c^v_s$ is invertible and does not identify $v^{-1}L_T$ with an inverse limit.

proof.text: The constant sheaf adjunction, composed with the given inverse-image adjunction, is the constant sheaf adjunction on the target because base change preserves a terminal object. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism. Its adjunct agrees with the specified constant direct-image map on the constant presheaf, so the actual constant inverse-image map is invertible. Sheafification uniqueness also proves naturality in the coefficient ring and the identity and composition laws for these direct-image maps.

source.place: Tags 00WX and 03CB; constant sheaf adjunction and uniqueness.

proof.text: Use the finite-root inverse-image theorem for transition compatibility and inverse-image semilinearity. For the finite direct-image maps, evaluate the specified root-section equivalence: their values are pullback of units along the fibre-product projection. Pullback of units respects the identity and composition comparisons by the fibre-product projection identities. The normalized constant finite-ring action makes every additive map between such modules linear; apply this to the direct-image root map.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03CB; root maps on units and normalized finite torsion actions.

proof.text: Compose each pulled-back limit projection with the compatible finite-root comparison. This is a cone over the target root tower, and its limit lift defines the root comparison. Take its adjunct to obtain c. The lift projection equations give c_projection; adjunction and the limit universal property give c_unique. Evaluate these equations on sections. Joint injectivity of limit projections, the finite identity/composition equations, and naturality of the projections prove the identity and composition equations for c. The recorded componentwise action and naturality of coefficient reduction prove its constant Z_l semilinearity.

source.place: Tags 03CO/03DB; universal property of the root inverse limit.

proof.text: Construct h directly in its displayed adjunct form. The semilinear map c sends x to the pure target tensor 1 tensor c(x); the coefficient naturality square makes this a linear map into the restriction of the direct-image tensor module. The scalar-extension universal property extends it uniquely. Its value on b tensor x is rho_B(b) tensor c(x). Equality of abelian sheaf maps out of scalar extension is detected on these original pure sections, by tensor generation before sheafification. Apply this test, coefficient identity/composition, root identity/composition, and restriction naturality to prove the all-section identity/composition equations.

source.place: Tag 03EK; scalar-extension universal property and pure-section formulas.

proof.text: If l^(r+1) kills B, the algebra map from Z_l to B kills the kernel of reduction to Z/l^(r+1). Its descended map is the unique ZMod cast homomorphism. The root projection is semilinear for this reduction, so scalar extension gives alpha with the prescribed pure formula. Construct d by the same scalar-extension lift applied to the finite direct-image root map. Both sides of the reduction square agree on every original pure section by c_projection, and scalar-extension extensionality gives equality of module morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EK; scalar factorization, finite tensor lift and projection square.
